claim: The west coast is sheltered from the Etesian/meltemi north winds while the south coast takes their full force; Mikri Vigla turns uncomfortable by 2pm in meltemi season.
quote: The west coast runs south from Naxos town in an almost unbroken line of fine golden sand, sheltered from the Etesian winds that blow hard from the north during summer. The south coast faces the open sea and takes the full force of those winds.

claim: Directory of Naxos beaches with distance from Chora, sand/pebble, organised vs non-organised, wind shelter and access mode for each.
quote: Agios Prokopios Beach ... 6 km southwest of Chora ... Protected from winds. Plaka Beach ... 8 km south of Chora ... Windy in meltemi season. Aliko ... 18 km south of Chora ... Car recommended.

claim: Agios Prokopios sunbed prices, bus time and fare, sheltered north-western stretch, and the walking connection to Agia Anna and Plaka.
quote: Front row runs around €30 per set, dropping toward the back and at the quieter western end of the strip. ... Head to the north-western public stretch which is more sheltered ... Line 1 from Chora costs €2.10, taking around 15 minutes.

claim: Plaka is the longest uninterrupted beach (4 km); Agios Georgios has a shallow sandy shelf; Kastraki gives sunset over Paros; Mikri Vigla is a dual-sided headland with sheltered Sahara to the south.
quote: the longest uninterrupted beach on the island ... Mikri Vigla: White sand; dual-sided headland; southern Sahara Beach sheltered ... North side catches meltemi winds

claim: Plaka is 4 km long, 8 km from Naxos Town, part-organised with tavernas and rentals behind the dunes, naturist in its southern sections, and has no organised parking.
quote: 4 km-long ... 8 km ... more pristine and secluded spots, where nudists still find their quiet corners ... no organized parking area

claim: Mikri Vigla is two beaches 250 m apart split by a rocky hill: Parthena on the north side for wind sports, Limanaki on the south; the coastal road includes dirt sections.
quote: On the north side of Mikri Vigla is Parthenos Beach, a small bay suitable for those who love water sports ... two consecutive beaches separated by a rocky hill ... 250 meters apart

claim: Limanaki, the southern half of Mikri Vigla, is well protected from north winds, has long wide golden sand, loungers and a couple of tavernas, and runs about 2 km toward Kastraki.
quote: white soft sand, azure color waters ... well protected from north winds ... loungers & sun umbrellas ... a couple of taverns

claim: Naxos Kitelife at Mikri Vigla cites 200+ windy days a year with dominant north winds, operates April to November and issues IKO certificates.
quote: more than 200 windy days per year ... dominant North winds ... In the end of your course with Naxoskitelife, you can get an IKO certificate to validate your level.

claim: Thalasea Sports sits on Mikri Vigla beach, is IKO-certified, runs April to November and prices private kite lessons from €85/hour, group from €95/hour for two.
quote: on the beach of Mikri Vigla ... every day from April to November ... Private kitesurf instruction starts at €85/hour, while group lessons begin at €95/hour for two people.

claim: Flisvos Kite Center is based at Orkos beach next to Mikri Vigla and runs a 10-hour IKO level 1+2 beginner course in groups of no more than two.
quote: Our basic kitesurf course IKO lev1 + lev2 is a 10 hours course with an IKO kitesurf instructor in a group never bigger than 2 persons.

claim: Mikri Vigla is roughly 16 km south of Naxos Town, wind is side-onshore, waves break on the beach and kiters and windsurfers share the same water.
quote: about 16 km south of Naxos-Town ... direction of the wind is side-onshore ... the surfing area is used by windsurfers and kitesurfers together

claim: Mikri Vigla's kite season is June to September, water is flat to choppy, a venturi effect between Naxos and Paros plus afternoon thermals boost the wind, and small kites are advised.
quote: From June to September ... Flat, choppy ... venturi effect created between Naxos and Paros islands, plus thermal winds ... bring small kite sizes

claim: Orkos is a chain of sandy coves ~10-11 km from Naxos Town, 15-20 minutes by car, reached on simple asphalt or dirt with informal roadside parking, no lifeguards, and used by riders as a quieter alternative to Mikri Vigla.
quote: roughly 10 to 11 kilometers from Naxos Town by road ... around 15 to 20 minutes ... Roads above the beach are simple asphalt or dirt, with cars parked informally along the shoulders ... no lifeguards stationed on the beach

claim: Kastraki is 15 km from Chora, fine white sand, mainly non-organised with a few sunbeds, shallow and windy, and reachable on bus Line 3.
quote: 15 km / 9.3 miles ... stunning fine white sand with crystalline waters ... Kastraki is mainly non-organized, but a few sunbeds are available along the shore ... it is too shallow and too windy

claim: Alyko is ~18 km from Chora on a paved road with a dirt/sand car park, has no sunbeds or umbrellas, rarely gets crowded, and Hawaii Beach is a 5-10 minute walk from the main cove; only food is the FBI food truck.
quote: roughly 18 kilometers from Naxos Town (Chora) ... a paved road that's easy to follow ... a dirt/sand parking lot ... Alyko Beach doesn't have sunbeds or umbrellas to rent ... rarely gets crowded

claim: The abandoned Alyko hotel was an unfinished resort whose concrete shells are now covered in murals and street art.
quote: The abandoned ruin hotel at the beach was once meant to be a 5 star resort but ran out of funds, so the built walls served as canvases for amazing murals, graffiti and street art.

claim: The Alyko cedar (juniper) forest covers the Kouroupia cape peninsula, roughly 1000 acres of dunes and trees, and is a reviewed visitor attraction in its own right.
quote: a unique forest of Junipers (Cedars), which covers almost the entire sandy peninsula of "Kouroupia" cape, with an extent of 1000 acres

claim: Agiassos is 23 km south of Chora, the last beach on the west side, protected from strong winds with shallow water safe for children, no sunbeds, 4 km from Pyrgaki and 5 km from Aliko.
quote: located 23 km south of Chora and it is the last beach on the western side of the island ... It is protected by strong winds whereas the shallow waters are safe for children ... No umbrellas or sunbeds are available at the beach

claim: Panermos is 54 km from Naxos Town and 17.5 km from Moutsouna, sandy with a few pebbles and palm shade, has one cafeteria and SUP rental, and is the departure point for mini-cruises to Rina.
quote: 54 km from Naxos Town ... a sandy beach with a few pebbles, crystal-clear waters, and a few palm trees for natural shade ... A boat tour that starts off Panermos carries out mini cruises to close beaches (like Rina)

claim: Rina Cave sits in the Kalandos area of southern Naxos, is reachable only by boat, is shielded from most winds and has stalactites sheltering birds and bats.
quote: It is located in the area of Kalandos, in the southern part of Naxos ... The cave is frequented by inflatable boats as the beach is shielded from most winds.

claim: A 2-hour traditional boat trip from Panermos to Rina Cave is bookable for the 2026 season.
quote: Naxos: Traditional Boat Trip to Rina Cave from Panermos - 2026

claim: Naxos Sailing runs a full-day Rina Cave and Small Cyclades sailing tour from Naxos port.
quote: Rina Cave & Small Cyclades - Naxos Sailing Daily Tours

claim: Rina Cave is also reachable on a guided sea-kayak day trip to Kalantos with snorkelling and a picnic.
quote: Rina Cave Sea Kayak Tour with Snorkeling and Picnic

claim: Psili Ammos on the east coast is ~44.2 km from Chora via Chalki-Filoti-Apiranthos on asphalt the whole way but narrow and winding after Apiranthos, with the final 150 m on foot or two wheels and no sunbeds.
quote: Asphalt road all the way. Narrow winding road after Apiranthos, extra driving care is necessary. ... For the next 150m access can be made by motorbike/scooter or on foot.

claim: Moutsouna is ~36.6 km from Chora via Chalki, Filoti and Apiranthos on a narrow winding road, has fine sand and seafront tavernas but no sunbed rental; Azalas is 1.5 km and Psili Ammos 8 km away.
quote: narrow winding road after Apiranthos, extra driving care is necessary ... No umbrellas or sun beds available for rent ... Azalas beach (1.5km), Psili Ammos beach (8km)

claim: Azalas is 37 km from Chora and 500 m from Moutsouna, now mostly pebbly, reached by a dirt road from Atsachas taking about 15 minutes, with no public transport and no facilities.
quote: The coast used to be sandy, but now it is mostly pebbly ... take the dirt road on the left ... around 15 minutes to arrive at the beach ... Tourism has not reached the area yet

claim: KTEL Line 1 (Town-Plaka) serves Agios Prokopios, Agia Anna, Plaka and Mikri Vigla from 07:30 to 01:00 with a 10-35 minute ride; Line 3 (Town-Pyrgaki) runs five times a day serving Mikri Vigla, Kastraki, Glyfada, Alyko and Pyrgaki in 15-55 minutes.
quote: Availability: From 07:30 to 01.00 and at 02.00 every day ... Price: €1.80 - €2.60 ... Duration: 10' - 35' ... Line 3 ... Availability: Five routes per day ... Duration: 15' - 55'

claim: The beach line runs roughly every 30 minutes in summer serving Agios Georgios through Mikri Vigla, tickets must be bought before boarding, and Alyko and Pyrgaki lack reliable bus service.
quote: Roughly every 30 minutes in summer, early until very late ... Buy the ticket before you board ... Alyko and Pyrgaki lack reliable bus service and require a car or taxi.

claim: The Naxos Town-Agios Prokopios-Agia Anna-Plaka line is the island's busiest and runs frequently all day in summer; remote east-coast coves and Panermos require private transport.
quote: the busiest route on the island ... in summer it runs frequently all day ... Remote east-coast coves and Panormos in the far south require private transport.

claim: Naxos roads are generally in good condition and a car suffices for Plaka, Alyko and Pyrgaki, but most rental contracts void insurance the moment you drive on dirt tracks or dunes; cars run about €25-40/day in shoulder season.
quote: Most rental contracts strictly forbid driving on dirt paths, rocky tracks, or dunes, and doing so can void your insurance instantly.

claim: Naxos roads are well maintained so cars and ATVs both work; ATVs reach narrower rugged tracks but cause accidents each year through speeding on turns.
quote: The roads throughout the island are well-maintained, which means cars and ATVs alike will get you where you want to be. ... accidents occur each year due to speeding and racing around turns
